subtitle: How a Learned Bahmani Sultan Carved Empire with Sword, Treaty and Tongue

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a throne hall fading into a battlefield and a script-covered sky
panels.action: Taj ud-Din Firuz Shah Bahmani sits on the Gulbarga throne, one hand resting on a sword, the other on a manuscript, as faint silhouettes of Raichur fort and Vijayanagara armies loom behind him and swirling calligraphic scripts hang like clouds.

dialogue.text: In the dusty Deccan between Gulbarga and Raichur, Sultan Firuz Shah Bahmani fought Vijayanagara by steel and treaty, and let many tongues—Persian and Dakhni, Kannada and Telugu—speak in his court.

i18n.hi: गुलबर्गा और रायचूर के बीच धूल भरे दक्खन में सुल्तान फ़िरोज़ शाह बहमनी ने विजयनगर से तलवार और सुलह से लड़ा, और अपने दरबार में फ़ारसी, दक्खनी, कन्नड़, तेलुगू – सब ज़बानों को बोलने दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a tense palace corridor at night
panels.action: Young Firuz, not yet crowned, stands half-shadowed in a torchlit corridor of Gulbarga fort, hand on the hilt of his sword, as armed courtiers murmur in clusters and a door to the royal apartments stands ajar.

dialogue.text: In 1397, the Bahmani palace at Gulbarga hissed with plots. When the old Sultan died, Ferishta says, rival princes and nobles moved in the corridors by torchlight, each weighing the throne in his own mind.

i18n.hi: १३९७ में, गुलबर्गा का बहमनी महल साज़िशों से सिसक रहा था। बूढ़े सुल्तान की मौत पर, फरीश्ता लिखता है, कि राजकुमार और अमीर मशालों के बीच गलियारों में घूम रहे थे, हर एक अपने मन में तख़्त तौल रहा था।

panels.shot: medium close-up profile of Firuz listening to two factions arguing in the shadows
panels.action: Firuz stands very still in a side chamber, profile calm yet alert, as two groups of nobles in different robes argue heatedly in the background, their fingers stabbing the air toward the throne room.

dialogue.text: Ferishta records a palace struggle. Firuz, son of Daud Khan and nephew of the first Bahmani, watched factions harden around other claimants, and knew that hesitation could cost his life.

i18n.hi: फरीश्ता महल की खींचतान दर्ज करता है। दौद ख़ाँ का बेटा और पहले बहमनी का भांजा फ़िरोज़ देख रहा था कि गुट दूसरे दावेदारों के इर्द-गिर्द सख़्त हो रहे हैं, और जानता था कि ज़रा-सी देर भी उसकी जान ले सकती है।

panels.shot: epic hall wide as Firuz steps toward the throne with armed supporters behind
panels.action: Inside the grand audience hall, Firuz strides steadily toward the vacant throne, a tight ring of mailed supporters around him, as other nobles freeze, hands half-reaching for their sword belts.

dialogue.text: The chronicles say he moved first. Backed by loyal amirs and soldiers, Firuz seized the palace, checked his rivals, and was proclaimed Sultan Taj ud-Din Firuz Shah Bahmani in Gulbarga.

i18n.hi: तवारीख़ कहती हैं, पहला क़दम उसी ने उठाया। वफ़ादार अमीरों और सिपाहियों के सहारे फ़िरोज़ ने महल पर क़ब्ज़ा किया, दुश्मनों को रोका, और गुलबर्गा में ताज-उद-दीन फ़िरोज़ शाह बहमनी के नाम से सुल्तान बना।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Firuz seated on the throne with books and weapons flanking him
panels.action: Firuz sits firmly on the Bahmani throne, a thick Persian codex on a stand to his right and a gleaming sword and bow set to his left, his gaze moving from scholar to officer standing before him.

dialogue.text: Unlike many warlords, Firuz had trained his mind as much as his arm. Ferishta praises him as a learned Sultan, and later scholars judge it plausible that he knew Arabic, Persian and Turkish, and learned the tongues of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: कई सरदारों के उलट, फ़िरोज़ ने दिमाग़ को भी बाँह जितना मज़बूत किया था। फरीश्ता उसे आलिम सुल्तान कहता है, और बाद के उलेमा मानते हैं कि उसे अरबी, फ़ारसी, तुर्की आती थीं, और उसने दक्खन की ज़बानें भी सीख ली थीं।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder view of Firuz speaking with two officials in different regional garb
panels.action: From behind Firuz, we see him addressing two officials in contrasting dress—one in northern-style robes, another in Deccan cotton and turban—while a map of the Raichur Doab lies open on the floor.

dialogue.speaker: taj_ud_din_firuz_shah_bahmani
dialogue.text: To hold this land, we must hear every tongue it speaks.

i18n.hi: ये धरती रखनी है, तो इसकी हर ज़बान सुननी होगी।

panels.shot: bird's-eye wide of the Deccan with Raichur Doab highlighted between two rivers
panels.action: A sweeping aerial view shows the twin rivers Krishna and Tungabhadra embracing the fertile Raichur Doab, with stylised Bahmani banners on one side and Vijayanagara emblems on the other facing each other across the land.

dialogue.text: Between the Krishna and Tungabhadra lay the Raichur Doab, rich in grain and taxes, key to war-horses from the west. Both Bahmani and Vijayanagara kings fought for it, year after year.

i18n.hi: कृष्णा और तुंगभद्रा के बीच पड़ा रायचूर दोआब, अनाज और लगान से भरपूर, पश्चिम से आने वाले घोड़ों की कुंजी – बहमनी और विजयनगर दोनों बादशाह हर साल इस पर जंग लड़ते रहे।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide of Bahmani army advancing toward Raichur fort
panels.action: Firuz rides at the head of armored horsemen across a dusty plain toward the looming walls of Raichur fort, with elephant corps and infantry stretching behind, banners snapping in the wind under a harsh Deccan sun.

dialogue.text: Ferishta describes Firuz leading repeated campaigns toward Raichur. Vijayanagara copper-plates confirm that on this frontier, in these years, Deccan and Kannada kings clashed in long, costly wars.

i18n.hi: फरीश्ता लिखता है कि फ़िरोज़ ने रायचूर की तरफ़ कई बार लश्कर खींचा। विजयनगर के तांबे के फ़रमान भी दिखाते हैं कि इसी सरहद पर, इन्हीं बरसों में, दक्खनी और कन्नड़ बादशाह लम्बी, महँगी लड़ाइयों में भिड़े।

panels.shot: close-up of Firuz on horseback surveying a smoking battlefield from a distance
panels.action: From his saddle on a rise, Firuz looks over a hazy battlefield where broken siege engines lie and distant fires smoulder near the walls, his face grave rather than exultant.

dialogue.text: Ferishta tells of desperate assaults and heavy losses, and gives vast casualty figures that historians now treat with caution. Whatever the exact numbers, the wars for Raichur bled men, money and grain on both sides.

i18n.hi: फरीश्ता बेबस हमलों और भारी जानी नुक़सान का ज़िक्र करता है, और ऐसी बड़ी तादाद देता है जिन्हें आज के इतिहासकार संभल कर देखते हैं। जो भी असली गिनती हो, रायचूर की जंगों ने दोनों तरफ़ के मर्द, माल और अनाज को लहू-लुहान कर दिया।

panels.shot: medium wide inside a Bahmani war council tent with maps and horse traders depicted
panels.action: Inside a campaign tent lit by oil lamps, Firuz leans over a rough map marked with the Raichur Doab, a line of coastal ports, and tiny horse symbols, while an Arab horse trader and a Deccan officer stand across from him.

dialogue.text: These were not only battles of creed. Ferishta notes disputes over territory and tribute, and the horse trade from the Arabian Sea. Control of the Doab meant feeding armies and buying cavalry from overseas.

i18n.hi: ये सिर्फ़ मज़हबी लड़ाइयाँ नहीं थीं। फरीश्ता इलाकों और नज़राने के झगड़े लिखता है, और अरब सागर से आने वाले घोड़ों के सौदे का भी ज़िक्र करता है। दोआब पर क़ब्ज़ा मतलब फ़ौज को खिलाना और समुंदर पार से सवार ख़रीदना।

panels.shot: tense frontal shot of Firuz and a Vijayanagara envoy facing each other in a pavilion
panels.action: Under a temporary pavilion on the frontier, Firuz sits straight-backed on a carpet while a Vijayanagara envoy in ornate South Indian attire stands across, both men framed by armed guards and a view of Raichur in the distance.

dialogue.speaker: taj_ud_din_firuz_shah_bahmani
dialogue.text: We can count dead men, or we can count seasons of peace.

i18n.hi: हम चाहें तो लाशें गिनें, या फिर अमन के मौसम।

panels.shot: symbolic split-panel style wide of a marriage procession and a frontier fort
panels.action: On one side of the frame a royal marriage procession with decorated palanquin and musicians moves forward; on the other, a distant frontier fort stands quiet under a calmer sky, suggesting a political alliance.

dialogue.text: After a hard-won victory over Vijayanagara, Ferishta mentions marriage ties sealing the peace. Modern historians read these as diplomatic alliances, binding frontier politics with family and dowry.

i18n.hi: विजयनगर पर सख़्त फ़तह के बाद, फरीश्ता निकाह के रिश्तों से सुलह की बात करता है। आज के इतिहासकार इन्हें कूटनीतिक गठजोड़ मानते हैं, जो सरहदी सियासत को परिवार और दहेज से बाँधते थे।

panels.shot: court wide of Gulbarga durbar with Hindus and Muslims standing together in official dress
panels.action: In the Gulbarga durbar, Firuz sits on the raised throne while rows of officials stand below—turbaned Muslim nobles beside Hindu courtiers in tilaks and regional garments—each holding petitions and revenue rolls.

dialogue.text: Ferishta notes that Firuz widened the circle of service. He brought more Hindu officers into his administration, tying local knowledge and loyalties to the Bahmani state, even as he rewarded his old Deccan companions.

i18n.hi: फरीश्ता लिखता है कि फ़िरोज़ ने ख़िदमत का घेरा बड़ा किया। उसने ज़्यादा हिंदू अफ़सरों को अपने इंतज़ाम में लाया, जिससे देसी ज्ञान और वफ़ादारी बहमनी हुकूमत से जुड़ गई, और साथ ही उसने अपने पुराने दक्खनी साथियों को भी इनाम दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Firuz listening to a Dakhni-speaking petitioner in simple clothes
panels.action: Firuz leans forward on the throne with a faint, attentive smile as a humble Deccan petitioner in coarse cotton speaks, gesturing nervously, while a scribe waits with reed pen and scroll beside them.

dialogue.text: Here, the language of power began to bend. Persian stayed the idiom of farmans and high poetry, but in the audience hall, Dakhni—the north Indian speech formed in the Deccan—grew louder beside it.

i18n.hi: यहीं क़ुदरत की ज़बान थोड़ा झुकने लगी। फ़ारसी अभी भी फ़रमानों और ऊँची शायरी की ज़बान रही, पर दरबार की हाज़िरी में दक्खनी – यानी दक्खन में बनी उत्तरी ज़बान – उसके साथ और बुलंद होने लगी।

panels.shot: intimate interior medium of Firuz writing by lamplight with multiple scripts around him
panels.action: By lamplight in a private chamber, Firuz sits cross-legged, reed pen in hand, writing on a small sheet while around him lie open pages in different scripts, their forms suggesting Persian and a more rounded Deccan hand.

dialogue.text: Later anthologies preserve Dakhni verses in his name. Scholars debate which lines are truly his, yet the very tradition remembers Firuz as a Sultan who not only ruled, but also wrote in the Deccan’s own speech.

i18n.hi: बाद की किताबें उसके नाम से दक्खनी अशआर सँजोती हैं। उलेमा बहस करते हैं कि कौन-सी पंक्तियाँ सच में उसकी हैं, पर ये रिवायत अपने आप कहती है कि फ़िरोज़ को ऐसा सुल्तान याद रखा गया जो सिर्फ़ हुक्म नहीं करता था, दक्खन की ज़बान में लिखता भी था।

panels.shot: visual metaphor wide of words flowing from palace into streets in different scripts
panels.action: Seen from above, Gulbarga’s palace towers over narrow streets as glowing calligraphic words in different scripts—suggesting Persian, Dakhni, Kannada and Telugu—flow from its gates into houses, shops and fields.

dialogue.text: Tariq Rahman and others place this Dakhni in the long story of Urdu. In the Deccan, under rulers like Firuz, a courtly, mixed speech slowly took shape, hearing both northern idioms and southern tongues.

i18n.hi: तारीक़ रहमान व दूसरे लोग इस दक्खनी को उर्दू की लम्बी कहानी में रखते हैं। दक्खन में, फ़िरोज़ जैसे हाकिमों के नीचे, एक दरबारी, मिली-जुली ज़बान धीरे-धीरे बनी, जो उत्तर की बोलियाँ और दक्खन की ज़बानें, दोनों सुनती थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of an older Firuz, thoughtful, with maps and books behind
panels.action: An older Firuz sits in semi-profile, face lined but eyes clear, with rolled maps of the Deccan and neatly stacked manuscripts behind him, as if weighing the memory of wars against the words he leaves behind.

dialogue.speaker: taj_ud_din_firuz_shah_bahmani
dialogue.text: Steel yields to rust. Words cross mountains.

i18n.hi: लोहा जंग खा जाता है, शब्द पहाड़ पार कर जाते हैं।

panels.shot: somber interior wide of Firuz’s bier surrounded by nobles of many communities
panels.action: In a dim hall, Firuz’s body lies on a simple bier draped in white, as nobles of varied dress and marks—Deccan Muslims, northern immigrants, and Hindu chiefs—stand at a respectful distance, heads bowed.

dialogue.text: Firuz Shah died in 1422, leaving a kingdom that would soon fracture. Yet in Ferishta’s pages and in Dakhni lines ascribed to him, he remains a ruler remembered for both campaigns and conversations.

i18n.hi: १४२२ में फ़िरोज़ शाह की मौत हुई, और पीछे ऐसा मुल्क छोड़ा जो जल्द बिखरने वाला था। पर फरीश्ता के सफ़ों में और उसके नाम से बची दक्खनी पंक्तियों में, वो आज भी ऐसे शासक के रूप में है जो जंगी मुहिमों के साथ गुफ़्तगू के लिए भी याद किया जाता है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Gulbarga and Bidar skylines dissolving into modern Deccan cities
panels.action: The domes and minarets of old Gulbarga and Bidar slowly dissolve into the skylines of modern Deccan cities, while translucent lines of multilingual scripts hover above roads, markets and crowded neighbourhoods.

dialogue.text: On the Bahmani frontier, Firuz Shah learned to wield languages like tools of state. His Deccan reminds us that when power listens in many tongues, it hears more of the land it claims.

i18n.hi: बहमनी सरहद पर फ़िरोज़ शाह ने ज़बानों को राज के औज़ार की तरह चलाना सीखा। उसका दक्खन याद दिलाता है कि जब ताक़त कई ज़बानों में सुनती है, तो उस धरती को ज़्यादा गहराई से सुनती है जिस पर दावा करती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Learned Bahmani Sultan Carved Empire with Sword, Treaty and Tongue
subtitle_i18n.hi: सीखे हुए बहमनी सुल्तान ने तलवार, सुलह और ज़बान से कैसे बनाया साम्राज्य
